Subject: Re: Private cutover today — intermittent upload failures

Hi Nikhil,

We cut over our on-prem link to Redwood’s private connector this morning. Since the cutover a subset of our VMs (internal services that push large attachments to our archival S3) are seeing intermittent upload failures and garbled payloads. The failures correlate with larger packets (10–20MB payloads) and show retransmits and ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages in the traces.

Our firewall logs also show a number of SG-tagged drops on the return path — the source IPs match Redwood edge SNAT pools but the firewall is classifying the responses as invalid. I’ve attached a short packet capture (zenith-cutover-trace1.pcap) and an extract of the SG logs (edge-sg-logs-20261114.log).

Can the Redwood team triage? We can schedule a maintenance window if you need to test changes (we have a 10:00–12:00 PT window Monday).

Thanks,
Alice Monroe

I pulled the pcap and logs. Quick notes: 
- The pcap shows ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) from an intermediate hop with MTU 1400. The client's SYN/handshake is with MSS ~1460, so without PMTU discovery or MSS clamp we'll see fragmentation.
- Our edge gateway is SNATing to 198.51.100.12/13 depending on flow hashing. I can see return traffic hitting a different edge chassis for some flows (route preference difference to Zenith's upstream). That explains the firewall invalid-state drops — packets are arriving at Zenith's firewall from an IP not associated with the original flow path.
- conntrack on the gateway shows entries but with mismatched nat_dst on some retransmits (likely due to asymmetric path and port remapping).

I recommend:
1) MSS clamp at the egress (TCP MSS 1360) as a short-lived mitigation.
2) Add a routing hint to prefer the original egress for Zenith's prefix while we validate (sticky route/flow pinning).
3) Temporarily add SG exception on Zenith side for established traffic from our SNAT ranges (they've offered to do this).

I will capture tcpdump on the gateway during the Monday window if allowed. Attaching a one-page plan (mss-clamp-proposal.md).

-Vanessa

Plan for Monday 10:00–11:00 PT (brief):

Step 0 — Pre-check (09:45)
- Snapshot current iptables/conntrack counters on private-gw-03. Save NAT table and route table.

Step 1 — Apply MSS clamp (10:00)
- Apply iptables rule: -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1360 on private-gw-03 (targeted to Zenith subnet filter).
- Validate with test uploads from a Canary VM and watch for 'fragmentation needed' ICMP disappear in tcpdump.

Step 2 — Route hinting (10:15)
- Add a sticky route for Zenith prefix to prefer edge-chassis-1 for the source SNAT range (BGP community export to our fabric or temporary static next-hop).

Step 3 — Coordination with Zenith (10:20)
- Zenith applies SG exception for established traffic from our SNAT block (they confirmed).

Step 4 — Observe (10:25–10:50)
- Monitor conntrack stability, upload success rates, and application logs. Capture 5-minute pcaps for verification.

Rollback (immediate)
- Remove MSS rule and route hint; restore snapshots.

Post-window (11:05)
- If successful for 30 minutes, remove MSS clamp and rely on route hint + SG fix for long-term. If issues persist, schedule host-level MTU changes with Zenith or longer-term permanent egress policy changes.

I’ll be on the call (Karthik). Chloe will run the captures and Vanessa will coordinate the gateway changes.

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: RESOLVED: Private cutover upload failures — actions and notes

Team — quick post-update: we executed the plan during the 10:00–11:00 PT window. Summary:
- MSS clamp (1360) applied on private-gw-03 targeted to Zenith prefix.
- Route hint made sticky to edge-chassis-1 for Zenith flows.
- Zenith applied SG exception for our SNAT range.

Result: upload failures stopped for the affected services during observation window; packet captures show no further ICMP fragmentation-needed and conntrack entries stabilized without nat_dst mismatches. We removed the MSS clamp after 45 minutes and traffic remained healthy using the route hint + SG fix.

Next steps:
- Add a short postmortem (owner: Chloe) documenting root cause: asymmetric egress path exposing differing MTU and SNAT mapping, causing firewall invalid-state drops.
- Engineering: consider permanent egress policy to keep prefix stickiness for similar private customers or implement L3 path MTU enforcement in the fabric. (Owner: Karthik).
- Ops: follow up with Zenith to roll a host-level MTU standardization if they prefer (Alice coordinating).

Thanks everyone for quick coordination. Closing INC-7890 pending Chloe's postmortem.

-Nikhil
